title: Toward Autonomous LLM-Based AI Agents for Predictive Maintenance: State of the Art, Challenges, and Future Perspectives
rationale: Review of LLM agents across the predictive-maintenance lifecycle; ties higher autonomy to needs for governance, benchmarks and safety evidence.

title: The Future of Research in an Artificial Intelligence-Driven World
rationale: Curated discussion of AI in the academic research process; no organizational process automation or control mechanism.

title: An ontology-guided approach to process formation and coordination of demand-driven collaborations
rationale: Ontology and semantic rules constrain generated BPMN executed by a workflow engine; deterministic process-constraint baseline with no LLM element.

title: DEVELOPMENT OF A BUSINESS PROCESS MODEL IN BPMN NOTATION FOR THE MANAGEMENT OF ROAD TRANSPORT OF A FREIGHT FORWARDING COMPANY
rationale: Russian-language BPMN model of freight-forwarding order fulfilment; non-English and no LLM or agentic component.

title: AI-Enhanced Business Process Automation: Integrating BPMN, DMN, and CMMN Standards for Enterprise Excellence
rationale: Argues for coupling AI decision-making to BPMN, DMN and CMMN process standards, the artifact class RQ1 tests, but reports no controlled evaluation.

title: Consensus speed of multi-agent systems driven by simultaneously fair value exchange
rationale: Control-theoretic consensus of incentive-driven multi-agent systems; keyword collision where agent is not an LLM.

title: A Conversational Assistant Framework for Automation
rationale: LLM assistant turns natural-language instructions into explicit workflows, decision rules and data models in watsonx Orchestrate, with empirical accuracy results.

title: From Intelligent Automation to Agentic AI: Engineering the Next Generation of Enterprise Systems
rationale: Reference architecture for agentic enterprise systems with autonomy and governance dimensions, AgentOps controls, and claimed gains over conventional intelligent automation.

title: Towards digital readiness of evidence-based practice in a regional cancer center using role-based business process and data modeling
rationale: BPMN and data modelling of nursing evidence-based practice for digital readiness; no LLM, no conformance checking or constraint semantics.

title: Evaluation of Automated Machinery Functional Safety Risk Assessment Using LLMs
rationale: Directly contrasts zero-shot natural-language prompting with prompts bound to the ISO 13849-1 decision graph, lifting safety-classification accuracy from under 50 percent to 99 percent.

title: AI-Powered Educational Agents: Opportunities, Innovations, and Ethical Challenges
rationale: Education-domain review whose finding that moderated hybrid workflows beat fully autonomous tutors is background for autonomy limits, not organizational process control.

title: Comparing Generative Chatbots Based on Process Requirements: A Case Study
rationale: Case study testing whether GPT and PaLM understand BPMN constructs well enough to support process execution, the exact model-binding question in RQ1.

title: Assessing business process models: a literature review on techniques for BPMN testing and formal verification
rationale: Review of BPMN testing and formal verification techniques for checking model compliance with requirements; anchors the deterministic baseline without any LLM.

title: LLM-driven big data management across digital governance, marketing, and accounting: A Spark-orchestrated framework
rationale: Fragmentary abstract on Spark-orchestrated LLM data management claiming compliance-critical settings; too little detail to extract a control mechanism.

title: <b>Business Process Automation: Compliance Management</b>
rationale: PLS-SEM survey of 270 employees on technology adoption and regulatory compliance; no LLM or agentic automation despite the title.

title: Pega Robotic Process Automation: Transforming Business Processes
rationale: Qualitative account of Pega RPA effects on compliance and efficiency; rule-based deterministic automation baseline with no LLM agency.

title: Robotic Process Automation in Business Process
rationale: Generic descriptive overview of RPA benefits with no method, result, or LLM or agentic element.

title: End-to-End Security Policy Automation with Multi-LLM Agents in Cloud-Native Systems
rationale: Multi-LLM agents generate machine-enforceable Istio access-control policies, benchmarked on five systems with unit tests and attack simulations; policy-as-artifact control mechanism.

title: Robotic Process Automation in Taxation
rationale: RPA automating tax compliance and reporting; deterministic rule-based baseline in a compliance-critical process, with no LLM or agentic reasoning.

title: GMATP-LLM: A General Multi-Agent Task Dynamic Planning Method using Large Language Models
rationale: Binds LLM chain-of-thought output to a PDDL model solved by a symbolic planner, the constrain-the-LLM mechanism class of RQ1, but in robotics rather than business processes.

title: Hierarchical LLM-Based Agent Framework for Natural Language-Driven Constraint-Aware Route Suggestion
rationale: Constraint-aware LLM agent for personal travel route suggestion; personal rather than organizational process.

title: Enhancing declarative business process management availability through generative AI
rationale: Constrained LLM generation with automated validation produces MP-Declare models supporting conformance checking; a control mechanism evaluated across 2000 models and two generation approaches.

title: Domain Agnostic Agentic AI: Enabling Autonomous Automation with SmartGenie CoPilot
rationale: Deployed agentic LLM copilot resolving employee service requests for a financial client, reporting completion-time and accuracy gains but no controlled baseline.

title: LLM Firewall Using Validator Agent for Prevention Against Prompt Injection Attacks
rationale: Validator agent acting as an output firewall performing policy-compliance verification and redaction; a named runtime guardrail with only viability-level evidence.

title: No-Code Automation Platforms for Incident Management: Transforming Engineering Operations
rationale: No-code visual workflow automation for incident management; explicit-workflow deterministic automation background with no LLM agency.

title: CAMEL: Communicative Agents for "Mind" Exploration of Large Language Model Society
rationale: Role-playing and inception prompting keep cooperating LLM agents aligned with human intent; foundational prompting-level control for multi-agent instruction following.

title: Large Process Models: A Vision for Business Process Management in the Age of Generative AI
rationale: States the RQ1 thesis directly, proposing Large Process Models that pair LLM correlation with symbolic process knowledge and automated reasoning for safety and trustworthiness.

title: RBPMN: the value of roles for business process modeling
rationale: BPMN 2.0 extension making roles and responsibilities explicit in process models; modelling-expressiveness background with no LLM or agentic element.

title: Generative AI and LLMs for Critical Infrastructure Protection: Evaluation Benchmarks, Agentic AI, Challenges, and Opportunities
rationale: Review of generative AI and agentic defence for critical infrastructure with LLM cybersecurity benchmarks; adjacent security background, not process compliance.

title: BPMN 2.0 to redefine Italian design-bid procurement in an innovative model-based, open-source approach
rationale: BPMN redefinition of Italian design-bid procurement; no LLM and no conformance-checking or constraint contribution.

title: Some Simple Economics of AGI
rationale: Economic argument that human verification bandwidth, not agent capability, binds automation; background for why oversight and auditability constrain agentic deployment.

title: BloombergGPT: A Large Language Model for Finance
rationale: Domain-specific financial LLM and its benchmarks; no agentic behaviour, process model, or compliance control.

title: Taming Uncertainty via Automation: Observing, Analyzing, and Optimizing Agentic AI Systems
rationale: AgentOps pipeline for observing and controlling agentic systems whose fluid execution paths create uncertainty; frames runtime control and issue detection without evaluation.

title: Agentic Services Computing
rationale: Service-centred roadmap for engineering and governing autonomous agents so they can be composed, monitored, audited and evolved as accountable services.

title: Intelligent AI Delegation
rationale: Delegation framework specifying authority, responsibility, accountability and role boundaries between agents and humans; a conceptual control mechanism for agentic work.

title: Developing trustworthy artificial intelligence: insights from research on interpersonal, human-automation, and human-AI trust
rationale: Psychological review of interpersonal, human-automation and human-AI trust; background for oversight and adoption, not a process-control mechanism.

title: Unraveling the Ethical Enigma: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare
rationale: Review of clinical AI ethics covering privacy, bias and responsibility; no agentic automation of an organizational process.

title: Large Language Models: A Structured Taxonomy and Review of Challenges, Limitations, Solutions, and Future Directions
rationale: Taxonomy of LLM limitations including interpretability, bias and control; general background on why LLM outputs need external constraint.

title: Model-Based System Engineering of the Internet of Things: A Bibliometric Literature Analysis
rationale: Bibliometric analysis of model-based systems engineering for IoT; BPMN is only a passing theme and there is no LLM or compliance angle.

title: Exploring the frontiers of LLMs in psychological applications: a comprehensive review
rationale: Review of LLM use in psychological research; wrong field with no organizational process or control mechanism.

title: Executable Digital Process Twins: Towards the Enhancement of Process-Driven Systems
rationale: Digital process twin monitoring and enacting system behaviour against a process specification; deterministic process-driven execution background with no LLM.

title: Design of blockchain-based applications using model-driven engineering and low-code/no-code platforms: a structured literature review
rationale: Review of model-driven and low-code platforms for blockchain applications; no LLM agency and no process-compliance question.

title: Editorial: Revolutionizing digital transformation in business and society through agentic AI integration
rationale: Editorial framing agentic AI as the answer to the enterprise generative-AI return-on-investment gap; adoption background with no mechanism or evidence.

title: A model-driven transformation approach for the modelling of processes in clinical practice guidelines
rationale: Transforms BPMN specifications into computer-interpretable clinical guidelines, encoding policy as an executable model; deterministic baseline with no LLM.

title: Giving texture to theory: A computational thought experiment on opportunity capital with LLM agents
rationale: LLM agents used as a computational thought experiment for entrepreneurship theory; no organizational process automation despite noting model sensitivity.

title: The Apologetic Authority: A Structural Critique of Anthropic's Constitution for Claude
rationale: Critique arguing that natural-language constitutional constraint obscures enforcement, auditability and traceability; conceptual background for the natural-language policy arm.

title: AI Security Priorities: A Field-Wide Agenda
rationale: Expert-elicited AI security agenda including a theme on governing agentic AI under adversarial pressure; priority-setting background rather than an evaluated mechanism.

title: Large language models for business and management applications: A review
rationale: Review of 84 LLM business and management applications mapping deployment patterns, retrieval grounding and governance-aware workflows plus persistent accuracy gaps.

title: Ethical perspectives on deployment of large language model agents in biomedicine: a survey
rationale: Survey cataloguing mitigation mechanisms for LLM agents including guardrailing, red-teaming and post-deployment monitoring, and their weak accountability evidence.

title: Business Process Modeled with BPMN and CTL Model Checking
rationale: Formal CTL model checking of BPMN models for soundness, fairness and safety; defines the verification baseline against which agent conformance can be judged.

title: BPMNE4IoT: A Framework for Modeling, Executing and Monitoring IoT-Driven Processes
rationale: BPMN extension for modelling, executing and monitoring IoT-driven processes with a user study; process-execution background with no LLM element.

title: GuardRails-as-Code and Audit Economics: Reducing Compliance Costs Through Policy Automation
rationale: Policy-as-code and compliance-as-code guardrails enforced in pipelines give continuous verifiable assurance; the machine-checkable policy alternative to natural-language rules.

title: ProtocolBench: Which LLM MultiAgent Protocol to Choose?
rationale: Benchmarks multi-agent communication protocols on task success, latency and failure recovery against single-protocol baselines; an evaluated coordination control at the infrastructure layer.

title: Actor-Driven Decomposition of Microservices through Multi-level Scalability Assessment
rationale: Actor-driven microservice decomposition and scalability assessment; software architecture method unrelated to LLM agents or process compliance.

title: Utilizing Large Language Models in Business Process Management: Applications and Challenges
rationale: Systematic review of 42 studies on LLMs across the BPM lifecycle, mapping which process tasks have been automated and the open interpretability and scalability gaps.

title: SOA Services Identification and Design Methods From Business Models: A Systematic Literature Review
rationale: Review of methods deriving service-oriented architectures from business models; architecture design rather than LLM agency or compliance control.

title: A Review of TRiSM Frameworks in Artificial Intelligence Systems: Fundamentals, Taxonomy, Use Cases, Key Challenges and Future Directions
rationale: Taxonomy of trust, risk and security controls for LLM systems including runtime enforcement and governance workflows across regulated domains.

title: A Review of Agentic Artificial Intelligence: Power of Self-Driven AI in the Future of Financial Autonomy and Enhanced Customer Engagement
rationale: Review of agentic AI for financial autonomy in an on-topic regulated domain, but the record carries only venue metadata and no usable abstract.

title: Defining Integrated Agriculture Information System Non-Functional Requirement and Re-engineering the Metadata
rationale: Maps non-functional requirements onto BPMN diagrams for an agriculture information system; requirements engineering with no LLM or conformance contribution.

title: Driving sustainable energy transitions with a multi-source RAG-LLM system
rationale: Retrieval-augmented energy question-answering chatbot for small enterprises; information retrieval rather than agentic process execution or policy control.

title: Generating Process Models by Interacting with Chatbots—A Literature Review
rationale: Review of chatbot-driven process model generation, mapping the natural-language to process-model interface that RQ1 depends on.

title: Business process modeling language selection for research modelers
rationale: Decision model for selecting among 23 business process modelling languages; background on the notation space that supplies the explicit process model.

title: Generative AI for Intelligent Manufacturing Virtual Assistants in the Semiconductor Industry
rationale: Deployed LLM agent assistant for semiconductor yield and defect analysis integrated with existing manufacturing systems; industrial evidence without compliance controls.

title: Machine Learning Techniques for Requirements Engineering: A Comprehensive Literature Review
rationale: Review of machine learning in requirements engineering; software development lifecycle rather than agentic automation of an organizational process.
